items.stem:
A teacher at Starlight Cinemas gives students recursive code to trace. (a) Compare the recursive and iterative solutions in terms of memory use and readability. (b) Write an iterative version of:
FUNCTION Product(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF N <= 1 THEN
        RETURN 1
    ELSE
        RETURN N * Product(N - 1)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.answer:
(a) Recursive uses a stack frame per call so more memory; iterative uses fixed memory; recursive often shorter/clearer. (b) FUNCTION Product(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    Result ← 1
    FOR i ← 2 TO N
        Result ← Result * i
    NEXT i
    RETURN Result
ENDFUNCTION

items.stem: Write pseudocode for a class Book for Starlight Cinemas with the private attributes Title : STRING, Author : STRING, Pages : INTEGER, a constructor that sets all the attributes from parameters, a getter for Title and a setter for Pages. The setter for Pages must only accept values from 0 to 1000 and return TRUE or FALSE.
items.answer:
CLASS Book
    PRIVATE Title : STRING
    PRIVATE Author : STRING
    PRIVATE Pages : INTEGER
    PUBLIC PROCEDURE NEW(pTitle : STRING, pAuthor : STRING, pPages : INTEGER)
        Title ← pTitle
        Author ← pAuthor
        Pages ← pPages
    ENDPROCEDURE
    PUBLIC FUNCTION GetTitle() RETURNS STRING
        RETURN Title
    ENDFUNCTION
    PUBLIC FUNCTION SetPages(NewPages : INTEGER) RETURNS BOOLEAN
        IF NewPages >= 0 AND NewPages <= 1000 THEN
            Pages ← NewPages
            RETURN TRUE
        ELSE
            RETURN FALSE
        ENDIF
    ENDFUNCTION
ENDCLASS
items.markingKey: 1 mark CLASS/ENDCLASS with PRIVATE attributes; 1 mark constructor NEW with parameters; 1 mark assignments; 1 mark getter; 1 mark setter with validation and return [1]

items.stem: Mohammed is writing a program for Starlight Cinemas that stores member names in a binary tree. (a) The values 22, 14, 85, 87, 82, 55, 75 are inserted in order. Give the in-order and post-order traversals. (b) Write a recursive pseudocode procedure InOrder(Node) that outputs the tree in order, using arrays LeftPointer, RightPointer and Data. (c) Explain why the tree may become slow to search over time.
items.answer:
(a) in-order 14, 22, 55, 75, 82, 85, 87; post-order 14, 75, 55, 82, 87, 85, 22 (b) PROCEDURE InOrder(Node : INTEGER)
    IF Node <> -1 THEN
        CALL InOrder(LeftPointer[Node])
        OUTPUT Data[Node]
        CALL InOrder(RightPointer[Node])
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE (c) If data is added in (nearly) sorted order the tree becomes unbalanced/tall, so searching approaches linear time.

Mei is comparing recursive and iterative solutions for Eagles Sports Club. (a) Compare the recursive and iterative solutions in terms of memory use and readability. (b) Write an iterative version of:
FUNCTION AddUp(Num : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Num = 0 THEN
        RETURN 0
    ELSE
        RETURN Num + AddUp(Num - 1)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.answer:
(a) Recursive uses a stack frame per call so more memory; iterative uses fixed memory; recursive often shorter/clearer. (b) FUNCTION AddUp(Num : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER

items.stem:
Rewrite this recursive function as an iterative function that gives the same result.
FUNCTION Remainder(Num : INTEGER, Step : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Num < Step THEN
        RETURN Num
    ELSE
        RETURN Remainder(Num - Step, Step)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.answer:
FUNCTION Remainder(Num : INTEGER, Step : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    WHILE Num >= Step
        Num ← Num - Step
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN Num
ENDFUNCTION

items.stem: Noah is comparing sorting algorithms for Atlas Museum's stock list. (a) Write pseudocode for an insertion sort on the array Scores[0:N-1]. (b) Explain which algorithm is better when one new score is added to an already sorted list.
items.answer:
(a) FOR i ← 1 TO N - 1
    Item ← Scores[i]
    j ← i - 1
    WHILE j >= 0 AND Scores[j] > Item
        Scores[j + 1] ← Scores[j]
        j ← j - 1
    ENDWHILE
    Scores[j + 1] ← Item
NEXT i (b) Insertion sort: the new item is moved into place in one pass (O(n)); bubble sort needs at least one full pass and may need more.
